stemMd: A grocery chain plans to replace paper shelf labels with electronic labels, claiming that labour savings will exceed the system’s annual cost. Which question is most useful in evaluating the claim?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Does the chain also sell stationery?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Are the electronic labels available in several colours?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Do shoppers recognize the chain’s logo?

options.label: D
options.textMd: How many years has the chain operated?

options.label: E
options.textMd: How many paid labour hours will actually be eliminated or productively reassigned because labels update electronically?

explanationMd: The claim depends on realized labour value, not merely faster label changes. A large usable time saving supports it; negligible redeployable time weakens it.

distractorRationale.a: Product category overlap does not settle the proposed economics.
distractorRationale.c: Recognition does not determine labour savings.
distractorRationale.b: Colour variety does not quantify the relevant benefit.
distractorRationale.d: Age alone does not compare the costs and savings.
